items.title: ragpicker
items.text:
ragpicker generates a self-contained, filesystem-based agentskills.io skill that wraps a haiku-rag-built LanceDB RAG database.

Unlike haiku-rag create-skill (which emits a haiku-skills entrypoint package consumed by haiku-rag's own pydantic-ai agent), the skill produced here is driven by an external agent (e.g. Claude Code) that invokes a script. The generated skill provides a PEP 723 wrapper, scripts/haiku_rag.py, exposing search and cite subcommands implemented over the haiku-rag Python client.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Given a haiku.rag.yaml config and a haiku-rag-built LanceDB database directory (<stem>.lancedb), ragpicker:

  • names the skill from the database directory stem (handbook.lancedb → handbook-haiku-rag);
  • copies the bundled template (shipped as package data under src/ragpicker/template/[dbname]-haiku-rag/), substituting [dbname] with the stem in path names and text-file contents;
  • embeds both the .lancedb database and the haiku.rag.yaml config under the skill's assets/;
  • pins an exact haiku-rag-slim version in the wrapper so the embedded database and the runtime always agree (see Version pinning).

items.title: Next steps
items.text:
• Ingesting documents — producing the database first: one-shot add-src, the haiku-ingester service, embedding models and docling-serve.
  • Generating a skill — the CLI and what it produces.
  • Version pinning — how the embedded database and runtime are kept in sync.

items.title: Generating a skill
items.text:
Assumes you already have a haiku.rag-built database; see Ingesting documents for producing and refreshing one.

uv run ragpicker \
    --config path/to/haiku.rag.yaml \
    --db path/to/handbook.lancedb \
    --output ./skills \
    [--haiku-rag-version 0.48.1 | --version-from-project path/to/stack]
  • The skill is named from the database directory stem: handbook.lancedb → handbook-haiku-rag.
  • The template under src/ragpicker/template/[dbname]-haiku-rag/ (bundled as package data) is copied with [dbname] substituted by the stem (in path names and text-file contents).
  • Both the .lancedb database and the haiku.rag.yaml config are embedded under the skill's assets/.

items.title: Using a generated skill
items.text:
cd handbook-haiku-rag
uv run scripts/haiku_rag.py search "<query>" [--limit N] [--filter "<SQL>"]
uv run scripts/haiku_rag.py cite <chunk_id> [<chunk_id> ...]

uv resolves the wrapper's pinned haiku-rag dependency on first use. The wrapper opens the bundled database read-only, so the embedded database and the pinned version always agree by construction (the generator either sniffs or migrates to match).

items.title: Embedding hosts (e.g. Soliplex)
items.text:
There are two execution models, with different requirements:

  • Standalone (uv run) — uv honors the wrapper's PEP 723 pin, so the runtime always matches the embedded database.
  • Embedding host (sys.executable) — a host such as Soliplex runs the skill script with its own Python interpreter, not uv (e.g. haiku.skills uses SCRIPT_RUNNERS[".py"] = (sys.executable,)). The wrapper's pin is then ignored: the host's installed haiku-rag opens the database. The embedded database must match that version, not the wrapper's pin.

So when targeting such a host, generate with --haiku-rag-version <the backend's haiku-rag version> (or --version-from-project) so the embedded database is migrated to match the interpreter that will open it. On a version mismatch the wrapper exits non-zero with an actionable haiku-rag version mismatch message instead of failing silently.

items.title: Ingesting documents
items.text: ragpicker wraps an existing database; it converts, chunks and embeds nothing itself. This page covers producing that database — the ingestion side of haiku.rag — before handing it to the generator. It targets haiku.rag 0.109.0 (current stable); younger features it relies on are marked with the release that added them.

items.title: One-shot: haiku-rag add-src
items.text:
haiku-rag init --db handbook.lancedb
haiku-rag add-src /srv/handbook-src/
haiku-rag search "attention mechanism"
  • add-src takes a file, a URL, a directory (walked recursively, ingesting every file whose extension docling or the text reader supports), or a s3:// object (requires the [s3] extra) — anything the ingester can watch, without setting the ingester up.
  • Re-ingesting an unchanged file is cheap: change detection by stored hashes skips the conversion/embedding entirely.

This is the whole story for a handbook that changes rarely or never.

items.title: Continuous: haiku-ingester
items.text:
For a corpus that keeps changing, a service watches sources and keeps the database in step: retries with backoff, a dead-letter queue, a control plane and a dashboard. Install the [ingester] extra (available since 0.50.0; the ingester.databases shape below needs 0.99.0+ — a configuration carrying the older ingester.sources fails to load on current releases):

pip install 'haiku.rag-slim[ingester]'   # or 'haiku.rag[ingester]'

Sources are configured under the database they feed:

lancedb:
  databases:
    handbook: ${HAIKU_RAG_CONFIG_DIR}/handbook.lancedb

ingester:
  databases:
    handbook:
      sources:
        - type: fs
          id: handbook
          root: /srv/handbook-src
          delete_orphans: true

haiku-ingester serve          # watch + sweep; control plane at 127.0.0.1:8765
haiku-ingester run-batch      # one sweep + drain, then exit: CI or cron
  • Source types: fs, http, s3, webdav, each with gitignore-style include/ignore filters and size limits. A per-source circuit breaker and a startup reconciliation between queue and store round out the machinery.
  • delete_orphans: true drops documents whose file has disappeared from the source; without it, stale documents stay searchable.
  • run-batch --dry-run writes a changeset manifest instead of ingesting; --manifest replays one frozen; --retry dead re-queues failures.
  • The control plane requires ingester.api.auth_token when it is not bound to loopback.

items.title: One writer per database
items.text: The ingester owns every database it writes; LanceDB allows exactly one writing process and any number of read-only consumers. Everything else — the MCP server, the generated skill — opens it read-only, and ragpicker's skill embeds a copy, so it never contends with the writer.

items.title: Picking and running an embedding model
items.text:
The embedder is configuration — embeddings.model in haiku.rag.yaml — and a plain CPU-only laptop is enough for any of these:

Option Shape Example Ollama (default) local server provider: ollama, name: qwen3-embedding:4b, vector_dim: 2560; ollama pull qwen3-embedding:4b In-process no server provider: sentence-transformers, name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2, vector_dim: 384 (cross-encoder extra, on haiku.rag) OpenAI-compatible localhost server provider: openai, base_url: http://localhost:1234/v1 (LM Studio, vLLM)

Rules that outlive the choice:

  • vector_dim must be the model's true output dimension and is frozen at database creation: the database records provider, model name, dimension and the optional query/document prefixes, and checks them on every open. Changing the model later is a haiku-rag rebuild, not a config edit.
  • The URL is not part of the recorded identity: pointing an existing database at the same model on a new host is a config edit alone.
  • Hosted embedders (voyageai, cohere, public APIs) work, but whatever runs the skill must reach the embedder at query time. Favor a localhost model when the skill will travel to hosts you do not control.
  • Only the embeddings section matters to a generated skill: its search/cite never calls the QA or reranking models.

items.title: Converting with docling-serve
items.text:
docling-local, the default converter, runs docling in-process and pulls the docling extra plus its layout/OCR models on first use — a heavy dependency for "Markdown in, search out". docling-serve offloads conversion (and chunking) to a REST service, so haiku.rag-slim runs without docling at all.

The upstream image runs docling on CPU, and Markdown/HTML corpora need no OCR in the first place, so a CPU-only localhost deployment is the sweet spot:

docker run -p 5001:5001 quay.io/docling-project/docling-serve:v1.38.2

processing:
  converter: docling-serve
  chunker: docling-serve

providers:
  docling_serve:
    base_url: http://localhost:5001
  • haiku.rag 0.109.0 is tested against docling-serve v1.38.2; pin the image tag to that release line.
  • do_ocr: false (the docling-serve chunker sends it along) skips OCR model downloads entirely for corpora whose text is already embedded.
  • docling-local remains the choice when pictures should come from the web: fetch_remote_images and its header controls exist only there — docling-serve stores picture_data=NULL for external <img> URLs.
  • The reference deployment is haiku.rag's examples/docker/ docker-compose.yml, which pairs the slim image (ghcr.io/ggozad/haiku.rag-slim, built with the ingester extra and without docling) with docling-serve replicas. Size ingester.workers.worker_count at 1–2× the number of base_url entries.

items.title: Checkup
items.text:
Before handing the database over — and any time it misbehaves — have haiku.rag examine its own work:

haiku-rag info --db handbook.lancedb     # snapshot: counts, sizes,
                                         # embedder, pending migrations
haiku-rag doctor --db handbook.lancedb   # pass/warn/fail report

doctor checks table correspondence, orphaned chunks and references, chunk vector dimensions, embedder identity agreement, index coverage and pending migrations, and probes the endpoints the configuration names (Ollama models present, docling-serve reachable, API keys set). Every finding names its remedying command (migrate, rebuild, create-index, vacuum, ...). --json prints a machine-readable report; --skip-providers skips both the API-key check and network probes. The haiku.rag web app runs the same report in its doctor page, for browser-only operators.

Details: https://ggozad.github.io/haiku.rag/cli/ (Database lifecycle: info, doctor).

items.title: From database to skill
items.text:
The skill embeds a snapshot copy: generation copies both the .lancedb directory and the haiku.rag.yaml config under the skill's assets/, leaving the ingester's database alone.

  • Quiesce the writer first: the directory copy is made with ordinary file copies, not atomically across tables. Right after a successful run-batch, or with serve briefly stopped, is safe.
  • Regeneration is the refresh path: when the ingester has ingested new content (or versions have moved), re-run ragpicker — the skill's copy gets replaced wholesale.
  • Generate with --version-from-project when the skill will run under an embedding host such as a Soliplex stack, so the embedded database matches the haiku-rag that interpreter will open it with (see Generating / Version pinning).
  • Verify the embedded config's embeddings.model agrees with the database's recorded identity (provider, name, vector_dim): a vector dimension mismatch refuses to open; a same-dimension mismatch warns and degrades retrieval. haiku-rag doctor performs the same check.

items.title: Version pinning
items.text:
The wrapper pins an exact haiku-rag-slim version so the embedded database and the runtime always agree. (Only haiku-rag-slim is supported — the full haiku-rag build's dependency weight is prohibitive for a self-contained skill.)

  • Default — sniff: the version is read from the database itself (the version that last wrote it, stored in its settings table) and pinned as-is. No migration is needed because the database already matches.
  • Minimum version: the wrapper's search/cite rely on APIs whose surface is not guaranteed below 0.48.1, so generation refuses to pin anything older. A database below that floor must be force-migrated up.
  • --haiku-rag-version X — force: X is pinned in the wrapper and the embedded copy of the database is migrated up to X (via uv tool run --from haiku-rag-slim==X haiku-rag migrate). The original database is left untouched. Downgrades are rejected (haiku-rag migrations only move forward).
  • --version-from-project PATH — discover + force: read the effective haiku-rag-slim version from a target project (e.g. a Soliplex stack) and force it the same way. Looks first in the project's .venv (the installed version), then falls back to resolving the project's dependencies with uv tree --package haiku-rag-slim --depth 0. Either path finds haiku-rag-slim even though it is a transitive dependency of soliplex (not named directly in pyproject.toml). Mutually exclusive with --haiku-rag-version.

Forcing requires uv on PATH and network access to fetch the requested version; most migrations are schema-only, but some may need model access.
